script.opening_words: You're in the Target checkout line with $67 worth of stuff you didn't come in for. There's a candle, paper towels, some kind of kitchen organizer that seemed essential 5 minutes ago. You don't remember what you actually came in for. And as the cashier scans the kitchen organizer, you feel it. That low-grade financial anxiety that has just become the background noise of your entire adult life. Not because you're broke, not because you're irresponsible, not because you bought
script.ending_words: a normal American in 2026, and it turns out that is a financially catastrophic thing to be. The cost of normal is $3.4 million. The cost of opting out is the mild social discomfort of driving a car that's paid off and canceling the gym membership you haven't used since February. That is the whole trade. The only question is whether anyone told you the trade existed. Now you know.
script.analysis: Full 18769 canonical characters read. A cost-of-living essay: Target checkout hook; "normal is a trap"; BLS CE total and categories (housing, transportation, food); car payments and prices, AAA ownership cost; food away from home and delivery fees; subscriptions; phone and internet; childcare; student loans; the Garcias budget; paycheck-to-paycheck at $100K and $500K; 30-year opportunity cost of the car, subscriptions and connectivity; why (car prices vs CPI, loan terms, subscription price creep, visibility trap); credit card debt; three actions (find your number, cut invisible overhead, spending gap); small-change compounding; close. Directly verified: BLS CE 2024 totals and categories (food $10,169 vs stated $10,164), CPI +88% since 2000. Contradicted by the same survey: "more on food away than groceries". Internally inconsistent: Garcias fixed costs ($4,713, not $5,093) and the "$275" margin. Saving rate 3.6% not supported by current-vintage data. Opportunity-cost and card-interest arithmetic reproduce. The stored ending is complete.

claim_audit.claim: The Garcias ($90,000, ~$6,000 take-home): itemised costs $4,333; after $380 student loans fixed costs $5,093; $907 left; $25,000 emergency fund takes over 2 years; 15% retirement is $1,125; "$275 of breathing room".

claim_audit.assessment: [INDEPENDENT_CALCULATION_VERIFIED] The ten items sum to $4,333 (reproduces). But $4,333 + $380 = $4,713, not $5,093, leaving $1,287, not $907 (the script adds $760). 25,000 / 907 = 27.6 months ("over 2 years") and 15% x 90,000 / 12 = $1,125 reproduce on its own numbers. The "$275" margin is never derived and contradicts $907. Internally inconsistent.
